title: Job aspirants protest in Patna over recruitment

tea.why: B Pharm graduates and Bihar Police driver candidates protested over recruitment issues and unallocated vacancies.
tea.want: B Pharm graduates seek inclusion in pharmacist recruitment, while driver candidates want vacant women's quota posts filled by men.
tea.changed: Oct 9: Police detained several job aspirants at Gandhi Maidan in Patna before a planned protest march.

summary: Job aspirants, including B Pharm degree holders and candidates for the Bihar Police driver recruitment, gathered at Gandhi Maidan in Patna to press for employment demands. The B Pharm graduates sought inclusion in the state pharmacist recruitment process. Meanwhile, the driver recruitment candidates demanded that over a thousand vacant posts reserved for women be allocated to eligible male applicants. Protesters had planned a march toward the Chief Minister's residence, but police intervened before the march began. Authorities deployed security personnel, erected barricades, and detained several individuals. While police stated the gathering was unauthorized, protesters claimed they had permission for a peaceful sit-in and march.
demands: Inclusion of B Pharm graduates in the state pharmacist recruitment process
Allocation of vacant posts reserved for women in the driver recruitment to eligible male candidates
response: Police detained several protesters at Gandhi Maidan and took them away in police vehicles, while some individuals were chased by officers. Gandhi Maidan SHO Akhilesh Kumar Mishra stated that the assembly was illegal and lacked permission.

updates.text: Police detained several job aspirants and B Pharm graduates at Gandhi Maidan before a proposed march.
